_comment: The vendor modules this machine has. Hand-maintained - it is the main repo's
single statement of which control platforms exist and which versions pair with
this one. A module is a SEPARATE repository the user clones into this repo's
root; the path is gitignored so the two git repos do not collide.
Four tools read this file: build_knowledge.py (which vendor links to emit),
build_wiki.py (which sibling wikis to link into, and where),
build_compatibility.py (the table, from the modules on disk) and
check_compatibility.py (the same pairing, asked of each module's own repository
over https - which is what CI runs, since it clones no module). Adding a vendor is
one entry here plus a repository - no tool changes.
`requires` is the module version range this main repo works with; `tested` is the
one it was actually verified against. Neither is derived - state them honestly.
`knowledgeBase` says whether the module publishes _docs/ pages that a root page
can link to - and therefore whether it has a wiki of its own to link into. It is
DECLARED rather than probed for, because these pages are tracked: deriving it from
what is on disk would make a tracked file's content depend on which optional
modules a given user happened to clone.
